questions.question: You are driving up a hill and see a heavy truck ahead. You should know that:

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often go slower than the speed limit on hills. Be careful when approaching a truck from behind. On a hill with limited visibility, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road is curving sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is curving sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the road curves sharply in the direction of the arrow (to the left). There may be several of these signs placed throughout the curve.

questions.question: You must drive carefully near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: He or she is deaf.
He or she is a police officer.
He or she is blind.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane means a pedestrian is blind. Slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to at a railroad crossing.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: When you see an accident scene, you should:

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Keep moving.
Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Only stop at an accident if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Keep watching the road and keep moving. Do not stop just to look at an accident, fire, or other disaster.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
If you are on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus shows flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop. Keep stopped as long as the red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: You are in an accident and someone is injured. You should:

options.text: Move the injured away immediately.
Always leave the injured where they are.
Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless necessary. Bad handling can turn minor injuries into serious ones. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop the flow.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the correct lane. You should:

options.text: Cut across traffic quickly to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Go to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes and put your vehicle in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the right lane to turn, drive to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while driving. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
Slam on the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: When power steering fails, you will need to use extra force to steer. Slow down and carefully pull off the road to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must come to a complete stop and let others pass.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and let others pass if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and let others pass if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangle sign means yield. Slow down at the intersection and be ready to stop. Let vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: What does a red and white triangular sign mean at an intersection?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways before crossing.
Always stop completely.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular yield sign means you must slow down and give the right-of-way to other vehicles and pedestrians. Be prepared to stop if necessary.

questions.question: You see a driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Keep extra space between you and that vehicle.
Know that this driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.
Do not copy this unsafe driving behavior.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space because they are more likely to crash.

questions.question: Which of these increases a driver's crash risk?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone, radio, or CD player can distract you and increase your risk of crashing.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they should:

options.text: Drive the same way as usual.
Drive faster because they are more alert.
Calm down and focus before starting to drive.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus before starting to drive.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions make it hard to drive safely. Your mind cannot focus on driving if you are upset. Take time to calm down before you start driving.

questions.question: You find a defect in your vehicle that could affect safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it right away.
Fix it when you have money.
Drive slower.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it right away.
questions.explanation: Any defect that affects safe driving must be fixed before you drive the vehicle.

questions.question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move ahead or drop back so they can see you.
Keep driving at the same speed.
Stay in their blind spot.
Honk your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move ahead or drop back so they can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not drive in someone's blind spot. Move ahead or back so the driver can see you.

questions.question: If your turn signals don't work, what should you use to signal a turn?

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: If your turn signals are broken, use hand signals to show when you are turning.

questions.question: Stopping completely, giving way to other traffic and pedestrians, then going through an intersection matches which traffic light?

options.text: A solid red light
A flashing yellow light
A solid green light
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians go, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: A flashing yellow light is coming
A steady green light is coming
A steady red light is coming
A flashing red light is coming

questions.correctAnswerText: A steady red light is coming
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light warns you that a red light will appear soon.

questions.question: How can you avoid a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive next to them and do not follow too close behind.
Flash your lights.
Use your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive next to them and do not follow too close behind.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have big blind spots on the sides and back. Do not drive beside them and do not tailgate.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a car crash?

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Limit your driving to weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the most effective way to reduce your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
Passing poor drivers by getting ahead of them in traffic.
Following the car in front of you closely.
Quickly changing lanes and weaving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you identify dangerous situations and take action before a crash happens. It helps you avoid problems with reckless, careless, or impaired drivers.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane when another driver passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help the passing vehicle get back into the right lane safely.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it is dangerous.
Lanes move in opposite directions.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: When must a vehicle buyer transfer ownership and registration?

options.text: By the end of the year.
Before the license plate expires.
Within 15 days of buying the vehicle.
Within 60 days of buying the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 15 days of buying the vehicle.
questions.explanation: A vehicle buyer must transfer ownership within 15 days to avoid penalty fees. If a dealer sells the vehicle, the dealer handles the transfer.
